results.title: ProtoNote: Share AI-built prototypes, get feedback pinned to the page | Product Hunt
results.content:
@better\_shaya Yeah, the loop is the whole problem. Feedback that isn’t attached to a specific spot on the page turns into a translation job, where you’re reading “the button feels off” and guessing which button. Pinning it means the note arrives with its own context, and once Claude can read those notes directly there’s no re-typing step at all. That last part is the piece I’m most curious to see people use. [...] 76 followers

76 followers

I build quick prototypes with Claude for a side project and used to just send people the raw HTML file or a Loom, then get back a one-line "looks good" that told me nothing. With ProtoNote I drop in the prototype, send the link, and people can leave notes pinned to the exact element instead of trying to describe where on the page something looks off. The part that actually saved me time is the Claude connector - I can tell it to pull in the open notes and it already knows exactly what element each one is talking about, so there's no back-and-forth translating "the button feels off" into something actionable. [...] I thought about just sharing a Figma link since most of the people I get feedback from already have accounts, but the prototypes I build with Claude aren't Figma files, they're actual working HTML, so I'd have to redo the whole thing in Figma just to get comments on it. ProtoNote takes the thing I already built as-is and skips that step entirely, plus reviewers don't need to make an account, which matters when I'm sending it to people outside my usual circle.

What do you think? …

As a Product Owners moving from Figma to Claude Code and constantly looking for feedbacks from stakeholders and testing users, this is life saver for me!
